Performers
Marine Chamber Orchestra, United States Marine Band (orchestra), Major Michelle A. Rakers (conductor) Documented

Commons gives the conductor as Major Michelle Rakers; the programme prints Major Michelle A. Rakers. No roster of individual players is published in the consulted sources. This video’s frames show the conductor and the strings; the ensemble’s harpsichord, bassoon and trumpet are visible in the other movements’ videos, and no frame shows horns or oboes.

[1] [4] [2]
Work version
Performing edition not identified. The movement number (14 of the three suites) and the structure heard (first strain of 19 bars played twice, second strain of 15 bars without brass, da capo to the fermata chord) match the Hallische Händel-⁠Ausgabe text; no editor or continuo realisation is credited. Inferred, not documented

The programme and Commons name the work and movement numbers but no edition. The structure follows from the measured silences and the Hallische Händel-⁠Ausgabe (Redlich, 1962), which prints 34 bars with a fermata, the mark Fine and a repeat sign at bar 19 and da capo at bar 34; IMSLP’s tally of 34 bars (53 with da capo) agrees.

[4] [7] [8] [6]
Recorded
2017-01-29 Documented

Commons gives performance_date 2017-01-29; the programme prints Sunday, January 29, 2017 at 2:00 P.M.; the official video description repeats the date. The Handel group stands after the intermission in the programme. The Commons composition_date field, 1717-07-17, is the date of the documented first performance on the Thames, not a composition date.

[1] [4] [2]
Place
Rachel M. Schlesinger Concert Hall and Arts Center, Northern Virginia Community College, Alexandria Campus, Alexandria, Virginia, United States Documented

Commons says Schlesinger Concert Hall, Alexandria, VA; the programme gives the full name of the hall and campus.

[1] [4]
Label
Unknown Unknown

No record label is identified. The source is an official concert video on the Marine Band’s YouTube channel; the channel is not treated as a label, and no commercial release was found.

[1] [2]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

No transfer or mastering engineer is identified. The Commons file history shows the batch upload by the user Mysterymanblue (pattypan), which is an uploader credit, not an engineering credit.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is documented. The YouTube publication date (30 April 2018) and the Commons upload date (28 June 2021) are not session or transfer dates.

[1] [2]
Processing
Opus audio file (48 kHz, two channels, encoder Lavf58.29.100) listed on Commons with the Marine Band’s YouTube playlist as its source; Commons supplies an MP3 access derivative. Inferred, not documented

The file’s own metadata documents the Opus format and encoder. That the audio was taken from the official video’s sound track is inferred from the source field and from the matching title and duration (136 s); the processing chain is not described.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Handel (died 1759): the composition is in the public domain. Documented

Commons tags the composition PD-old-auto-expired (death year 1759). The performing edition is not identified; editorial copyright in a modern edition, if one was used, is separate from the sound recording.

[1]
Recording rights
Commons tags the performance and recording PD-USGov-⁠Military-⁠Marines: a work of a United States Marine or employee made as part of official duties, public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government. Documented

This is a U.S.-jurisdiction statement, not a claim of worldwide status. The programme carries a general notice that a performance may contain third-party material and should not be assumed to be public domain; no third-party material is identified in this performance of a composition from before 1759, but the notice is recorded here. The official Marine Band YouTube channel published the source video.

[1] [5] [2]

George Frideric Handel, Water Music, Suite No. 2 in D, HWV 349: III. Lentement. Marine Chamber Orchestra of the United States Marine Band, Major Michelle Rakers conducting; Rachel M. Schlesinger Concert Hall, Alexandria, Virginia, 29 January 2017. Audio via Wikimedia Commons from the official Marine Band concert video. U.S. federal-government work; public domain in the United States. Rights statement
